close_reason: Wire literal at task_list.rs:247 changed to spec-canonical singular form. All tests updated to use independent spec oracle (draft-ietf-jmap-tasks-06 §3.4 line 691) instead of self-oracling. cargo fmt + clippy + test green. Commit 51354c8.
description: draft-ietf-jmap-tasks-06 §3.4 (line 691) defines the SetError type as 'taskListHasTask' (singular). The implementation in crate-jmap-tasks-server/src/task_list.rs:247 emits 'taskListHasTasks' (plural). Tests in src/task_list.rs:337, src/lib.rs:659, tests/tasks_tests.rs:193 assert the plural form — they pass because they self-oracle against the implementation, violating the workspace test-integrity policy that the spec is the oracle. PLAN.md correctly cites the singular form. Trigger: any TaskList/set destroy with onDestroyRemoveTasks=false against a list that has tasks. Bad behavior: clients pattern-matching SetError.type against the draft will not match the response; the violation is silent (no top-level error). Fix: change the literal at task_list.rs:247 to 'taskListHasTask'; update assertions in three test files to use the singular form; cross-check PLAN.md and README.md (README also uses plural at lines 97/143/184). Note: this is the only crate-defined SetError type for TaskList/set destroy, so no other code depends on it.
title: wire-protocol bug: taskListHasTasks should be taskListHasTask per draft-tasks-06 §3.4
